subject: Hierarchical models with varying number of indicator variables for the FOLVs

messages.author: 570debbdb91283e7
messages.subject: Hierarchical models with varying number of indicator variables for the FOLVs
parts:
Dear all

I wonder whether it's possible to construct hierarchical models when the number of indicator variables for each FOLV varies.  In my hypothetical model, there would be 19 FOLVs (the concept is a complex one), indicated from anything to 1 variable in a couple of cases to 16 in others.  Is such a model statistically feasible?  Perhaps also worth noting that the data is nearly all in Likert-type scales, or dichotomous.  I have attached a sketch of the first 7 FOLVS - the page would be a lot wider if I was sketch the whole thing.  Also each SOLV is hypothesised to influence each other (is this possible when specifying the relationship between FOLVs?

Any thoughts/opinions on this greatly appreciated!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Hierarchical models with varying number of indicator variables for the FOLVs
parts: I wonder whether it's possible to construct hierarchical models when the number of indicator variables for each FOLV varies.

There is no assumption about latent variables having the same number of indicators.  Special constraints are needed when you have only 1 or 2 indicators of a factor, but all latent variables in your model (first- or second-order) can have different numbers of indicators.
Is such a model statistically feasible?

Only if you have a very large sample size, so that your model converges and the parameter estimates are estimated with any decent amount of precision.  I wouldn't feel comfortable fitting a model with 19 FOLVs using any less that N = 2000 on the small side (I base that on intuition and previous experience, with no data to support that number -- there is free literature available on simulation-based power analyses using Mplus).
Perhaps also worth noting that the data is nearly all in Likert-type scales, or dichotomous.
That might be a problem for LVs with only 1 indicator (I don't think that can be identified).

I have attached a sketch of the first 7 FOLVS - the page would be a lot wider if I was sketch the whole thing.  Also each SOLV is hypothesised to influence each other (is this possible when specifying the relationship between FOLVs?

Yes.  The second-order "factor loadings" are in the Beta matrix, with all the  other latent-variable regression coefficients.  So there is no statistical distinction between a second-order factor loading and a latent regression slope, just in how you interpret them (although that is how you interpret loadings -- as slopes). 


Since this is a general SEM question rather than a lavaan issue, it would be more appropriate to post this on SEMNET.  That might also be advantageous for you, as it has been around longer and has a larger audience of people who could help.

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html

Terry

parts:
Dear Terrence

Thanks for your detailed reply, much appreciated.

1. What are the special constraints for 1 or 2 indicators per factor?  From what I've read so far, I would guess this is about constraining the residual variances.  Any good sources on this?  For categorical variables, presumably if there are only 1 or 2 indicators, then I could just model these without latent variables (but they can still be specified to have the same types causal relationships right?)

2. The data is European Social Survey data which has about n=2000 per country, so I may just about be ok with this, but will soon know whether the models converge or not.

3. SEMNET sounds like a useful resource - I'll take a look!

Regards, Dan.
